chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whoever conceals his fast, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to His angels: 'My servant seeks refuge from My punishment, so grant him refuge.' And Allah, the Exalted, has assigned His angels to supplicate for the fasting ones, and He did not command them to supplicate for anyone except that He answers them regarding it.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for concealing one's fast in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Shia emphasis on *khum al-sawm* (concealing the fast) as a mark of sincere *ikhlas*, distinguishing it from the Sunnah practice of publicizing it. It illustrates a unique divine mechanism where Allah delegates the intercession for the fasting servant to His angels, ensuring their supplications are invariably accepted, thereby linking private devotion directly to heavenly endorsement.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who conceals his Fast, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Says to His<sup>azwj</sup> Angels: “My<sup>azwj</sup> servant seeks Refuge from My<sup>azwj</sup> Punishment, so I<sup>azwj</sup> hereby Grant him Refuge”, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted Allocates His<sup>azwj</sup> Angel with supplicating for the Fasting ones, and He<sup>azwj</sup> does not Command them with the supplication for anyone except that He<sup>azwj</sup> Answers for them with regards to it’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father, from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

if a person fasts secretly, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, says to His angels, ‘My servant has sought protection against my punishment, you must give him protection.’ Allah, the most Blessed, the most High, then assigns His angels to pray for the fasting people and in whoever’ s favor He commands them to pray, He hears and accepts their prayers.’”
